detail.longDescription: Update. # OpenAI just announced a new policy on how to release new results produced by its # AI tools in # mathematics , # computerscience , and # physics . https:// openai.com/index/building-scie ntific-understanding-with-academic-communities/ It will consult with human experts called "shepherds" and will apparently ask them about # OpenAccess , timing, and ways to help the disciplinary communities digest the results. Here I'll focus on the # OA piece. The decision is clearest in # CS : "Mak[e] the AI output publicly available for anyone to examine and build on." I'd call that OA. Presumably the OA release would be on # arXiv or # GitHub . For physics, the decision is uncertain: "Form an external group of collaborators and defer to them on the release of materials." Apparently members could decide against any release, against early release, and/or against OA release. For # math , the decision is hazy: "Release the AI output." OK, but in public? For everyone? It's so easy to say "in public for everyone" that we wonder whether the omission is significant. As I read the announcement, OpenAI is taking three divergent approaches more in the spirit A/B testing than to respect disciplinary differences. "We do not yet know which of these three approaches will be most useful, and we welcome feedback on what works and what we can improve."
